76:   |
77:   +-- exact skill name or explicit user direction -> named skill wins
78:   |
79:   +-- non-trivial or ambiguous request
80:         |
81:         +-- advisor_recommend through the advisor CLI
82:         |
83:         +-- top recommendation above confidence threshold -> invoke that skill
84:         |
85:         +-- ambiguous top scores -> surface top candidates and ask or route with caveat
86: ```
87: 
88: Resource domains:
89: 
90: - `references/scoring/` documents scorer lanes, lane weight tuning, calibration and validation baselines.
91: - `references/graph/` documents skill graph queries, drift reconciliation, graph extraction status and `enhances` propagation.
92: - `references/runtime/` documents the CLI front-door contract, stable command ids, freshness and daemon lease behavior.
93: - `references/config/` documents package-local database path policy.
94: - `hooks/` documents prompt-time hook behavior across runtimes.
95: - `references/decisions/` documents deferred decision records and historical rationale that still affects operators.
96: - `feature-catalog/` documents current advisor capabilities and source-of-truth feature references.
97: - `manual-testing-playbook/` documents deterministic operator scenarios for advisor tools, hooks, compatibility, daemon behavior and skill graph flows.
98: - `runtime/` owns handlers, schemas, tools, scripts, tests, library modules and the package-local SQLite database.
99: 
100: **Typed leaf projection (fleet routing standard).** system-skill-advisor is a normal, standalone single-mode skill. Its sole workflow mode is `system-skill-advisor`, and there is no `mode-registry.json`.
101: 
102: - Every routable leaf under the five declared leaf roots, `references/`, `assets/`, `feature-catalog/`, `manual-testing-playbook/` and `hooks/`, is enumerated in `leaf-manifest.json`, generated from `leaf-manifest.config.json` and narrowed by `leaf-scopes.json`.
103: - `hooks/` is Markdown-only through `leaf-scopes.json`: the scope names its five hook docs, and the nine runtime `.ts`, `.py` and `.json` files beside them are never leaves. `assets/` is declared and has no docs to contribute.
104: - Regenerate both generated class-S artifacts with `node .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-skill/scripts/ci-skill-root-metadata.cjs --fix`.
105: - The plain gate must keep them byte-stable.
106: - `leaf-aliases.json` binds each router-emitted root-relative path (e.g. `references/scoring/advisor-scorer.md`) to its typed `(system-skill-advisor, leafResourceId)` identity. A deterministic router replay recovers real typed pairs against the manifest.
107: - The `RESOURCE_MAP` below emits those exact leaf paths.
108: - The feature-catalog and manual-testing-playbook package indexes are navigation only. They are never routed as typed leaves.
109: - Do not hand-edit either generated file.
110: - The `runtime/` advisor engine (`skill-graph.json`, scorer/prompt-policy config, handlers) is the runtime, not a routable documentation leaf. It is intentionally outside every `leafRoot` and never appears in the manifest.
111: 
112: ### Resource loading levels
113: 
114: | Level | When to Load | Resources |
115: |---|---|---|
116: | FALLBACK | Request too weak to score | The two `DEFAULT_RESOURCES` runtime references, offered with the disambiguation checklist (fallback-only: never unioned into a scored route) |
117: | SELECTED | An intent scores | The exact `RESOURCE_MAP[intent]` leaf(s) for the selected intent(s), emitted as typed `(WORKFLOW_MODE, leafResourceId)` pairs |
118: | NAVIGATION | Broad "list the features / playbook" browse | A `PACKAGE_INDEXES` index doc: navigation only, never a typed leaf |
119: 
120: ### Smart router pseudocode
121: 
122: The prompt-time brief can show a runnable `/doctor:` command as the top line or as an `Also:` second line under a skill.
123: 
124: This pseudocode is the canonical resource-routing contract. The router is a singleton-mode selector:
125: 
126: - It scores the request against `INTENT_SIGNALS`.
127: - It keeps the intents within the ambiguity delta of the top score, at most two.
128: - It resolves each intent to its exact `RESOURCE_MAP` leaf path. Use no directory prefixes, filename stems or globs.
129: - Every selected leaf projects to a typed `(WORKFLOW_MODE, leafResourceId)` pair against `leaf-manifest.json` via `leaf-aliases.json`.
130: - Package indexes and fallback defaults ride their own channels. They never become typed leaves.
131: - The live advisor scorer, not this router, remains authoritative for runtime skill scoring. See [`references/scoring/advisor-scorer.md`](./references/scoring/advisor-scorer.md).
132: 
133: ```python
134: from pathlib import Path
135: 
136: SKILL_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
137: RESOURCE_BASES = (
138:     SKILL_ROOT / "references",
139:     SKILL_ROOT / "assets",
140:     SKILL_ROOT / "feature-catalog",
141:     SKILL_ROOT / "manual-testing-playbook",
142:     SKILL_ROOT / "hooks",
143: )
144: 
145: # This standalone skill emits exactly one workflow mode. Every routed leaf is a
146: # (WORKFLOW_MODE, leafResourceId) pair. leaf-manifest.json is the authorized
147: # leaf inventory; leaf-aliases.json binds each router-emitted path to its typed
148: # identity so a deterministic benchmark replay recovers real pairs.
149: WORKFLOW_MODE = "system-skill-advisor"
150: 
151: # Always-relevant runtime references offered when a request is too weak to
152: # score. DEFAULT_RESOURCE_SEMANTICS = "fallback-only": the defaults are a
153: # defer-time suggestion surfaced with the disambiguation checklist, never
154: # unioned into a scored route's typed leaves, so selected-leaf precision holds.
155: DEFAULT_RESOURCES = [
156:     "references/runtime/tool-ids-reference.md",
157:     "references/runtime/standalone-mcp-shape.md",
158: ]
159: DEFAULT_RESOURCE_SEMANTICS = "fallback-only"
160: 
161: # Navigation indexes: loadable for browsing, deliberately excluded from typed
162: # leaves and from leaf-manifest.json. A broad "list the features / playbook"
163: # request loads these; they never become a (mode, leaf) pair.
164: PACKAGE_INDEXES = {
165:     "FEATURES": "feature-catalog/feature-catalog.md",
166:     "PLAYBOOK": "manual-testing-playbook/manual-testing-playbook.md",
167: }
168: 
169: # Intent -> weighted keyword signals. Keys are honest documentation-topic
170: # vocabulary drawn from what each reference/feature doc is ABOUT, not reverse
171: # engineered from any scenario prompt. A distinctive doc phrase scores weight 3;
172: # there are no per-scenario exact-match keys, so measured routing recall stays
173: # an honest reflection of natural topic overlap rather than a tuned number.
174: INTENT_SIGNALS = {
175:     "SCORER": {"weight": 3, "keywords": ["scorer", "lane fusion", "five-lane", "confidence calibration", "lane attribution", "ambiguous brief", "ambiguity window"]},
176:     "LANE_TUNING": {"weight": 3, "keywords": ["lane weight tuning", "reweight lane", "lane weight change"]},
177:     "VALIDATION_BASELINES": {"weight": 3, "keywords": ["validation baseline", "advisor_validate baseline", "validate slice bundle"]},
178:     "GRAPH_QUERY": {"weight": 3, "keywords": ["skill graph query", "skill_graph_query", "graph query cookbook", "skill graph status", "skill graph validate", "relationship read"]},
179:     "GRAPH_DRIFT": {"weight": 3, "keywords": ["skill graph drift", "reconcile graph drift", "sqlite drift"]},
180:     "GRAPH_EXTRACTION": {"weight": 3, "keywords": ["graph extraction plan", "extraction history", "extraction completion"]},
181:     "ENHANCES": {"weight": 3, "keywords": ["propagate enhances", "enhances propagation", "skill_graph_propagate_enhances"]},
182:     "MCP_SHAPE": {"weight": 3, "keywords": ["standalone mcp shape", "mcp topology", "server shape", "standalone advisor mcp"]},
183:     "TOOL_IDS": {"weight": 3, "keywords": ["tool id", "stable tool id", "tool ids reference"]},
184:     "LEGACY_BRIDGE": {"weight": 3, "keywords": ["legacy tool bridge", "compatibility bridge", "bridge policy"]},
185:     "FRESHNESS": {"weight": 3, "keywords": ["freshness contract", "trust state", "trust-state vocabulary", "degraded daemon", "quarantined daemon", "unavailable daemon"]},
186:     "DAEMON_LEASE": {"weight": 3, "keywords": ["daemon lease", "single-writer lease", "lease contract", "chokidar watcher", "daemon lifecycle"]},
187:     "DB_PATH": {"weight": 3, "keywords": ["database path policy", "sqlite path", "db path"]},
188:     "HOOK": {"weight": 3, "keywords": ["skill advisor hook", "prompt-time hook", "userpromptsubmit", "opencode plugin bridge", "goal opencode plugin"]},
189:     "DECISIONS": {"weight": 3, "keywords": ["deferred decision", "tier d", "deprecation banner"]},
190:     "RECOMMEND": {"weight": 3, "keywords": ["advisor_recommend", "recommend happy path"]},
191:     "STATUS": {"weight": 3, "keywords": ["advisor_status", "status transition", "status and rebuild"]},
192:     "REBUILD": {"weight": 3, "keywords": ["advisor_rebuild", "rebuild from source"]},
193:     "VALIDATE_TOOL": {"weight": 3, "keywords": ["advisor_validate"]},
194:     "CLI": {"weight": 3, "keywords": ["skill-advisor cli", "daemon-backed cli", "cli fallback"]},
195: }
196: 
197: # Intent -> exact leaf path(s). No prefixes, stems, or globs: every value is a
198: # concrete markdown leaf that exists in leaf-manifest.json (package indexes are
199: # intentionally absent — they live in PACKAGE_INDEXES). Several intents share a
200: # reference leaf on purpose; the many feature-catalog and playbook leaves that
201: # no intent maps stay reachable only via PACKAGE_INDEXES or a full-inventory
202: # browse. That unmapped remainder is expected, not a gap to be closed by tuning.
203: RESOURCE_MAP = {
204:     "SCORER": ["references/scoring/advisor-scorer.md"],
205:     "LANE_TUNING": ["references/scoring/lane-weight-tuning.md"],
206:     "VALIDATION_BASELINES": ["references/scoring/validation-baselines.md"],
207:     "GRAPH_QUERY": ["references/graph/skill-graph-query-cookbook.md"],
208:     "GRAPH_DRIFT": ["references/graph/skill-graph-drift.md"],
209:     "GRAPH_EXTRACTION": ["references/graph/skill-graph-extraction-plan.md"],
210:     "ENHANCES": ["references/graph/propagate-enhances.md"],
211:     "MCP_SHAPE": ["references/runtime/standalone-mcp-shape.md"],
212:     "TOOL_IDS": ["references/runtime/tool-ids-reference.md"],
213:     "LEGACY_BRIDGE": ["references/runtime/legacy-tool-bridge.md"],
214:     "FRESHNESS": ["references/runtime/freshness-contract.md"],
215:     "DAEMON_LEASE": ["references/runtime/daemon-lease-contract.md"],
216:     "DB_PATH": ["references/config/db-path-policy.md"],
217:     "HOOK": ["hooks/skill-advisor-hook.md"],
218:     "DECISIONS": ["references/decisions/deferred-decisions.md"],
219:     "RECOMMEND": ["feature-catalog/cli-surface/advisor-recommend.md"],
220:     "STATUS": ["feature-catalog/cli-surface/advisor-status.md"],
221:     "REBUILD": ["feature-catalog/cli-surface/advisor-rebuild.md"],
222:     "VALIDATE_TOOL": ["feature-catalog/cli-surface/advisor-validate.md"],
223:     "CLI": ["feature-catalog/cli-surface/skill-advisor-cli.md"],
224: }
225: 
226: UNKNOWN_FALLBACK_CHECKLIST = [
227:     "Confirm whether the request is about scoring, skill graph, runtime, config, hooks, decisions, the command surface, features or playbooks",
228:     "Confirm whether the task changes documentation only or executable advisor behavior",
229:     "Provide the failing tool id, hook runtime, reference path or validation command",
230:     "Confirm the verification command set before completion",
231: ]
232: 
233: def discover_markdown_resources() -> set[str]:
234:     docs = []
235:     for base in RESOURCE_BASES:
236:         if base.exists():
237:             docs.extend(path for path in base.rglob("*.md") if path.is_file())
238:     return {doc.relative_to(SKILL_ROOT).as_posix() for doc in docs}
239: 
240: def _guard_in_skill(relative_path: str) -> str:
241:     resolved = (SKILL_ROOT / relative_path).resolve()
242:     resolved.relative_to(SKILL_ROOT)  # fail closed on any escape
243:     if resolved.suffix.lower() != ".md":
244:         raise ValueError(f"Only markdown resources are routable: {relative_path}")
245:     return resolved.relative_to(SKILL_ROOT).as_posix()
246: 
247: def _task_text(task) -> str:
248:     fields = [
249:         getattr(task, "prompt", ""),
250:         getattr(task, "intent", ""),
251:         getattr(task, "path", ""),
252:         getattr(task, "command", ""),
253:     ]
254:     return " ".join(str(field) for field in fields if field).lower()
255: 
256: def score_intents(task) -> dict[str, int]:
257:     text = _task_text(task)
258:     scores = {}
259:     for intent, model in INTENT_SIGNALS.items():
260:         hits = sum(1 for keyword in model["keywords"] if keyword in text)
261:         if hits:
262:             scores[intent] = hits * model["weight"]
263:     return scores
264: 
265: def typed_leaves(paths: list[str]) -> list[dict]:
266:     # Project selected leaf paths into deduped (workflowMode, leafResourceId)
267:     # pairs. Package indexes are never present (they are not in RESOURCE_MAP);
268:     # a path that is not a real manifest leaf is dropped, never emitted as an
269:     # invented pair.
270:     seen, pairs = set(), []
271:     index_paths = set(PACKAGE_INDEXES.values())
272:     for path in paths:
273:         if path in index_paths or (WORKFLOW_MODE, path) in seen:
274:             continue
275:         seen.add((WORKFLOW_MODE, path))
276:         pairs.append({"workflowMode": WORKFLOW_MODE, "leafResourceId": path})
277:     return pairs
278: 
279: inventory = discover_markdown_resources()
280: scores = score_intents(task)
281: 
282: # Too weak to score: offer the fallback defaults + disambiguation and assemble
283: # no typed leaves. DEFAULT_RESOURCE_SEMANTICS = "fallback-only" is exactly what
284: # makes the defaults a suggestion here rather than an assembled route.
285: if max(scores.values() or [0]) < 3:
286:     return {
287:         "workflowMode": WORKFLOW_MODE,
288:         "load_level": "UNKNOWN_FALLBACK",
289:         "needs_disambiguation": True,
290:         "disambiguation_checklist": UNKNOWN_FALLBACK_CHECKLIST,
291:         "supportResources": [p for p in DEFAULT_RESOURCES if p in inventory],
292:         "leafResources": [],
293:     }
294: 
295: # Keep intents within the ambiguity delta of the top score (at most two). A
296: # genuine tie between equally weighted keys surfaces both; otherwise the single
297: # top intent resolves to exactly its own leaf.
298: ranked = sorted(scores.items(), key=lambda item: item[1], reverse=True)
299: top_score = ranked[0][1]
300: selected = [intent for intent, score in ranked if top_score - score <= 1][:2]
301: 
302: resources = []
303: for intent in selected:
304:     for path in RESOURCE_MAP.get(intent, []):
305:         guarded = _guard_in_skill(path)
306:         if guarded in inventory and guarded not in resources:
307:             resources.append(guarded)
308: 
309: return {
310:     "workflowMode": WORKFLOW_MODE,
311:     "intents": selected,
312:     "ambiguous": len(selected) > 1,
313:     # Compatibility flat list: selected leaves only. Fallback defaults are NOT
314:     # unioned in (fallback-only semantics), so a scored route carries exactly
315:     # its intents' leaves.
316:     "resources": resources,
317:     # Typed projection every benchmark/replay consumer compares byte-for-byte.
318:     "leafResources": typed_leaves(resources),
319:     # Support defaults and navigation indexes ride their own channels so they
320:     # never inflate selected-leaf precision.
321:     "supportResources": DEFAULT_RESOURCES,
322:     "navigationResources": PACKAGE_INDEXES,
323: }
324: ```
325: 
326: ### Fallback contract
327: 
328: - **Low confidence:** load default runtime references, emit `UNKNOWN_FALLBACK_CHECKLIST`, and ask for the missing intent/path/tool signal.
329: - **Ambiguous intent scores:** load the top two intents' exact leaves and disclose the ambiguity instead of picking one silently.
330: - **Known intent with no mapped leaf:** return a "no knowledge base found" notice naming the missing intent. Never invent a typed pair for a path outside `leaf-manifest.json`.
331: - **Advisor daemon unavailable:** Run `node .skilled/bin/skill-advisor.cjs advisor_recommend --json '{"prompt":"<request>"}' --format json`.
332:   - The CLI starts the daemon when the socket is cold.
333:   - If the daemon stays unreachable, the CLI answers from the local Python scorer and marks the result degraded. The brief then renders `Advisor: stale` instead of claiming live.
334:   - A degraded answer is stale. A missing answer is a fail-open.
335:   - Prompt-time adapters cap the call with their own timeout and never block the prompt.
336:   - Operator checks, doctor routes and scripts use the same CLI with `--timeout-ms N`.
337:   - Direct callers that need the Python JSON-array shape use `runtime/scripts/skill_advisor.py`.
338:   - The full command contract, output envelope, exit taxonomy and stale-build recovery are in [`references/runtime/cli-front-door-contract.md`](./references/runtime/cli-front-door-contract.md).
339: 
340: ### Gate 2 caller guidance
341: 
342: - Use `node .skilled/bin/skill-advisor.cjs advisor_recommend --json '{"prompt":"<request>"}' --format json` for live runtime routing. The CLI is the only front door.
343: - Use `runtime/scripts/skill_advisor.py` for the JSON-array facade contract: compatibility scripts and callers that parse the Python output shape.
344: - Exit `75` is retryable fail-open: bound the call with a timeout and continue without a recommendation rather than blocking. The CLI cold-starts the daemon and bounds the wait itself.
345: - CLI calls are sent untrusted by default. Mutations (`advisor_rebuild`, `skill_graph_scan`, apply-mode `skill_graph_propagate_enhances`) require `--trusted` or `SYSTEM_SKILL_ADVISOR_CLI_TRUSTED=1`, the maintainer path. Read commands never need it.
346: 
347: ### Anti-patterns
348: 
349: - Directory prefixes, filename stems, or globs in `RESOURCE_MAP`. Every value is an exact leaf path that exists in `leaf-manifest.json`.
350: - Tuning `INTENT_SIGNALS` keywords to make individual scenario prompts hit their own leaf. Keys are documentation-topic vocabulary. A low honest routing recall is expected, not a defect to be inflated.
351: - A hand-maintained resource inventory that drifts from `leaf-manifest.json`. Regenerate both generated class-S artifacts with `node .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-skill/scripts/ci-skill-root-metadata.cjs --fix` instead of synchronizing either file by hand.
352: - Raw `load("references/file.md")` calls without `_guard_in_skill()`, inventory checks or duplicate suppression.
353: - Hardcoded tool IDs in caller code. Consult the live definitions in `runtime/tools/index.ts` and `runtime/tools/skill-graph-tools.ts`.

31: # System Skill Advisor
32: 
33: Routes non-trivial user requests to the right skill through the standalone Skill Advisor package and its CLI front door.
34: 
35: ---
36: 
37: ## 1. WHEN TO USE
38: 
39: Use this skill when the work is about skill selection, Gate 2 routing, advisor CLI commands, prompt-time skill-advisor hooks, skill graph freshness or the standalone advisor package.
40: 
41: Activation signals:
42: 
43: - A request asks which skill should handle a task.
44: - A runtime hook needs a skill recommendation before execution.
45: - An operator asks about `advisor_recommend`, `advisor_status`, `advisor_rebuild`, `advisor_validate`, `skill_graph_scan`, `skill_graph_query`, `skill_graph_status`, `skill_graph_validate` or `skill_graph_propagate_enhances`.
46: - A packet touches the skill graph, skill metadata, advisor scorer, advisor feature catalog or manual testing playbook.
47: 
48: Do not use this skill as a replacement for the recommended target skill. For example, route code implementation to `sk-code`, documentation authoring to `sk-doc`, git work to `sk-git` and MCP orchestration to `mcp-code-mode` after the advisor has made the recommendation.
49: 
50: ---
51: 
52: ## 2. SMART ROUTING
53: 
54: Use this skill for non-trivial Gate 2 routing or requests about advisor commands, hooks, skill graph or the package.
55: An exact skill name or explicit user direction takes priority.
56: Otherwise, use `advisor_recommend` through the CLI to choose a target skill.
57: Load that target skill before acting in its domain.
58: This package covers advisor routing and behavior.
59: For local documentation, load the leaf mapped to the detected intent.
60: Weak signals use fallback references. Broad browsing uses a package index.
61: Read [`ROUTER.md`](./ROUTER.md) before selecting skill-local resources; open only the matched files.
62: 
63: ---
64: 
65: ## 3. HOW IT WORKS
66: 
67: The advisor runs as a resident daemon with one CLI front door. The package owns the whole routing boundary, so routing can be tuned and rolled back independently.
68: 
69: The package owns the advisor daemon and its CLI front door, and it lists all **9 commands**. The command ids stay stable:
70: 
71: Commands (9):
72: 
73: - `advisor_recommend`
74: - `advisor_rebuild`
75: - `advisor_status`
76: - `advisor_validate`
77: - `skill_graph_scan`
78: - `skill_graph_query`
79: - `skill_graph_status`
80: - `skill_graph_validate`
81: - `skill_graph_propagate_enhances`
82: 
83: `skill_graph_propagate_enhances` is trust-gated only for real apply writes (`mode=apply` with `dryRun` not `true`). Report, propose and dry-run apply calls remain read-safe.
84: 
85: The stable command ids matter because live consumers already call them from hooks, the Python scorer, doctor workflows, scripts and CI. The package boundary supplies the isolation, so callers use the advisor without learning a new vocabulary.
86: 
87: The CLI is the only front door. The same 9 commands are callable through `node .skilled/bin/skill-advisor.cjs <command>` over the daemon's unix socket. A shim refuses to run a stale dist.
88: Recovery example: `node .skilled/bin/skill-advisor.cjs advisor_recommend --json '{"prompt":"<request>"}' --format json --timeout-ms 3000`.
89: Exit codes:
90: - `0`: success.
91: - `1`: runtime.
92: - `64`: usage/schema or trusted-mutation refusal.
93: - `69`: protocol/dist mismatch or stale dist.
94: - `75`: retryable daemon error.
95: 
96: - When the daemon is unreachable, the CLI answers from the local Python scorer and marks the result degraded instead of failing the call.
97: - `--format jsonl` renders one complete JSON payload on one stdout line. It is not streaming JSON Lines.
98: - Trust resolution fails closed. A call is untrusted unless `--trusted` or `SYSTEM_SKILL_ADVISOR_CLI_TRUSTED=1` is supplied. Mutation commands therefore require the maintainer path.
99: 
100: **Routing phrases come from `graph-metadata.json`.** The daemon routes from each skill's `graph-metadata.json` using `intent_signals` and `derived.trigger_phrases`.
101: 
102: - The create-skill metadata CI check keeps that file aligned with the skill root.
103: - The `trigger_phrases` and `intent_signals` fields in a skill's `SKILL.md` frontmatter are not read by any runtime routing reader.
104: - The local Python scorer's frontmatter cache reads only `name`, `description` and an inline `keywords` value.
105: - Reference and asset doc frontmatter `trigger_phrases` feed routing only when `SPECKIT_ADVISOR_DOC_TRIGGERS=true`.
106: - Skill authors change routing vocabulary in `graph-metadata.json`.
107: 
108: `advisor_status` reports `indexStaleness` on every successful call and, with `includeEmbeddingsHealth`, an opt-in `embeddingsHealth` covering provider resolution and the local model server.
109: 
110: The advisor implementation, skill-graph library and package-local database live under this skill package, while memory remains focused on memory tools.
111: 
112: **Skill lifecycle: how a new skill becomes routable.**
113: 
114: 1. The daemon watcher monitors the skills root itself. It watches that root shallowly, covering top-level directories only. It also watches each known root's identity files.
115: 2. When a skill is created while the daemon is warm, the new directory's event goes through the normal debounce into reindex.
116: 3. Reindex promotes the root's `SKILL.md`, `ROUTER.md` and `graph-metadata.json` into durable watch targets.
117: 4. With no daemon running, the next daemon start ingests the skill through normal discovery.
118: 5. Refresh manually at any time with `node .skilled/bin/skill-advisor.cjs skill_graph_scan --trusted`.
119: 6. Deleting a root retires its targets through the same path.
120: 7. The authoring-side counterpart (routing-evidence quality and the discovery smoke test) lives in the create-skill workflows.
121: 
122: ---
123: 
124: ## 4. RULES
125: 
126: ### ALWAYS
127: 
128: - Treat `references/runtime/cli-front-door-contract.md` as the source of truth for command ids, output shape and exit codes.
129: - Keep the advisor database under `.skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/database/`.
130: - Keep public advisor and skill graph command ids stable unless a later ADR explicitly changes them.
131: - Preserve prompt-safety boundaries. Advisor metadata and lane attribution must not echo raw prompt text.
132: - Keep `runtime/lib/skill-graph/` package-local to `system-skill-advisor`.
133: 
134: ### NEVER
135: 
136: - Store `skill-graph.sqlite` outside this package. The database is package-local.
137: - Let any other runtime or server write the advisor SQLite database.
138: - Rename `advisor_*` or `skill_graph_*` public commands as part of documentation work.
139: - Move `runtime/lib/skill-graph/` during a doc-only pass.
140: 
141: ### ESCALATE IF
142: 
143: - A caller requires renamed public tools.
144: - The standalone advisor cannot build without a broader shared-runtime extraction.
145: - Any migration step would create competing writers for `skill-graph.sqlite`.

31: # System Skill Advisor
32: 
33: Routes non-trivial user requests to the right skill through the standalone Skill Advisor package and its CLI front door.
34: 
35: ---
36: 
37: ## 1. WHEN TO USE
38: 
39: Use this skill when the work is about skill selection, Gate 2 routing, advisor CLI commands, prompt-time skill-advisor hooks, skill graph freshness or the standalone advisor package.
40: 
41: Activation signals:
42: 
43: - A request asks which skill should handle a task.
44: - A runtime hook needs a skill recommendation before execution.
45: - An operator asks about `advisor_recommend`, `advisor_status`, `advisor_rebuild`, `advisor_validate`, `skill_graph_scan`, `skill_graph_query`, `skill_graph_status`, `skill_graph_validate` or `skill_graph_propagate_enhances`.
46: - A packet touches the skill graph, skill metadata, advisor scorer, advisor feature catalog or manual testing playbook.
47: 
48: Do not use this skill as a replacement for the recommended target skill. For example, route code implementation to `sk-code`, documentation authoring to `sk-doc`, git work to `sk-git` and MCP orchestration to `mcp-code-mode` after the advisor has made the recommendation.
49: 
50: ---
51: 
52: ## 2. SMART ROUTING
53: 
54: Use this skill for non-trivial Gate 2 routing or requests about advisor commands, hooks, skill graph or the package.
55: An exact skill name or explicit user direction takes priority.
56: Otherwise, use `advisor_recommend` through the CLI to choose a target skill.
57: Load that target skill before acting in its domain.
58: This package covers advisor routing and behavior.
59: For local documentation, load the leaf mapped to the detected intent.
60: Weak signals use fallback references. Broad browsing uses a package index.
61: Read [`ROUTER.md`](./ROUTER.md) before selecting skill-local resources; open only the matched files.
62: 
63: ---
64: 
65: ## 3. HOW IT WORKS
66: 
67: The advisor runs as a resident daemon with one CLI front door. The package owns the whole routing boundary, so routing can be tuned and rolled back independently.
68: 
69: The package owns the advisor daemon and its CLI front door, and it lists all **9 commands**. The command ids stay stable:
70: 
71: Commands (9):
72: 
73: - `advisor_recommend`
74: - `advisor_rebuild`
75: - `advisor_status`
76: - `advisor_validate`
77: - `skill_graph_scan`
78: - `skill_graph_query`
79: - `skill_graph_status`
80: - `skill_graph_validate`
81: - `skill_graph_propagate_enhances`
82: 
83: `skill_graph_propagate_enhances` is trust-gated only for real apply writes (`mode=apply` with `dryRun` not `true`). Report, propose and dry-run apply calls remain read-safe.
84: 
85: The stable command ids matter because live consumers already call them from hooks, the Python scorer, doctor workflows, scripts and CI. The package boundary supplies the isolation, so callers use the advisor without learning a new vocabulary.
86: 
87: The CLI is the only front door. The same 9 commands are callable through `node .skilled/bin/skill-advisor.cjs <command>` over the daemon's unix socket. A shim refuses to run a stale dist.
88: Recovery example: `node .skilled/bin/skill-advisor.cjs advisor_recommend --json '{"prompt":"<request>"}' --format json --timeout-ms 3000`.
89: Exit codes:
90: - `0`: success.
91: - `1`: runtime.
92: - `64`: usage/schema or trusted-mutation refusal.
93: - `69`: protocol/dist mismatch or stale dist.
94: - `75`: retryable daemon error.
95: 
96: - When the daemon is unreachable, the CLI answers from the local Python scorer and marks the result degraded instead of failing the call.
97: - `--format jsonl` renders one complete JSON payload on one stdout line. It is not streaming JSON Lines.
98: - Trust resolution fails closed. A call is untrusted unless `--trusted` or `SYSTEM_SKILL_ADVISOR_CLI_TRUSTED=1` is supplied. Mutation commands therefore require the maintainer path.
99: 
100: **Routing phrases come from `graph-metadata.json`.** The daemon routes from each skill's `graph-metadata.json` using `intent_signals` and `derived.trigger_phrases`.
101: 
102: - The create-skill metadata CI check keeps that file aligned with the skill root.
103: - The `trigger_phrases` and `intent_signals` fields in a skill's `SKILL.md` frontmatter are not read by any runtime routing reader.
104: - The local Python scorer's frontmatter cache reads only `name`, `description` and an inline `keywords` value.
105: - Reference and asset doc frontmatter `trigger_phrases` feed routing only when `SPECKIT_ADVISOR_DOC_TRIGGERS=true`.
106: - Skill authors change routing vocabulary in `graph-metadata.json`.
107: 
108: `advisor_status` reports `indexStaleness` on every successful call and, with `includeEmbeddingsHealth`, an opt-in `embeddingsHealth` covering provider resolution and the local model server.
109: 
110: The advisor implementation, skill-graph library and package-local database live under this skill package, while memory remains focused on memory tools.
111: 
112: **Skill lifecycle: how a new skill becomes routable.**
113: 
114: 1. The daemon watcher monitors the skills root itself. It watches that root shallowly, covering top-level directories only. It also watches each known root's identity files.
115: 2. When a skill is created while the daemon is warm, the new directory's event goes through the normal debounce into reindex.
116: 3. Reindex promotes the root's `SKILL.md`, `ROUTER.md` and `graph-metadata.json` into durable watch targets.
117: 4. With no daemon running, the next daemon start ingests the skill through normal discovery.
118: 5. Refresh manually at any time with `node .skilled/bin/skill-advisor.cjs skill_graph_scan --trusted`.
119: 6. Deleting a root retires its targets through the same path.
120: 7. The authoring-side counterpart (routing-evidence quality and the discovery smoke test) lives in the create-skill workflows.
121: 
122: ---
123: 
124: ## 4. RULES
125: 
126: ### ALWAYS
127: 
128: - Treat `references/runtime/cli-front-door-contract.md` as the source of truth for command ids, output shape and exit codes.
129: - Keep the advisor database under `.skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/database/`.
130: - Keep public advisor and skill graph command ids stable unless a later ADR explicitly changes them.
131: - Preserve prompt-safety boundaries. Advisor metadata and lane attribution must not echo raw prompt text.
132: - Keep `runtime/lib/skill-graph/` package-local to `system-skill-advisor`.
133: 
134: ### NEVER
135: 
136: - Store `skill-graph.sqlite` outside this package. The database is package-local.
137: - Let any other runtime or server write the advisor SQLite database.
138: - Rename `advisor_*` or `skill_graph_*` public commands as part of documentation work.
139: - Move `runtime/lib/skill-graph/` during a doc-only pass.
140: 
141: ### ESCALATE IF
142: 
143: - A caller requires renamed public tools.
144: - The standalone advisor cannot build without a broader shared-runtime extraction.
145: - Any migration step would create competing writers for `skill-graph.sqlite`.

13: # System Skill Advisor DB Path Policy
14: 
15: Open this policy when verifying the SQLite path or evaluating a test/CI override.
16: 
17: ---
18: 
19: ## 1. OVERVIEW
20: 
21: ### Purpose
22: 
23: Defines the package-local SQLite database location for the standalone advisor runtime and documents the allowed test/CI override behavior.
24: 
25: ### When to Use
26: 
27: - Verifying where `skill-graph.sqlite` and lease sidecars must live.
28: - Reviewing a database path change, launcher change or runtime ownership question.
29: - Checking whether a proposed override is limited to tests and CI.
30: 
31: ### Core Principle
32: 
33: The advisor owns its SQLite state inside `system-skill-advisor`; adjacent packages must not become competing writers.
34: 
35: ### Key Sources
36: 
37: - `runtime/lib/skill-graph/skill-graph-db.ts`
38: - `runtime/database/README.md`
39: 
40: ---
41: 
42: ## 2. POLICY
43: 
44: The advisor database lives inside the standalone advisor skill package:
45: 
46: ```text
47: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/database/skill-graph.sqlite
48: ```
49: 
50: It must not live under:
51: 
52: ```text
53: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/database/
54: ```
55: 
56: SQLite sidecars stay beside the database file:
57: 
58: ```text
59: skill-graph.sqlite-wal
60: skill-graph.sqlite-shm
61: ```
62: 
63: ---
64: 
65: ## 3. RATIONALE
66: 
67: ADR-001 constraint A requires DB-local ownership for the extracted advisor. The database is the advisor's runtime state, so it belongs with the skill that reads, writes, validates and rebuilds it.
68: 
69: This separation gives cleaner mutation scope:
70: 
71: - `/doctor:skill-advisor rebuild` and future repair flows can reason per skill package.
72: - The advisor daemon is the single writer for `skill-graph.sqlite`.
73: - `system-spec-kit` keeps memory and spec packet state without owning advisor runtime data.
74: - Backups, cleanup and integrity checks can target the advisor package directly.
75: 
76: ---
77: 
78: ## 4. TEST AND CI OVERRIDE
79: 
80: - `SYSTEM_SKILL_ADVISOR_DB_DIR` is allowed for tests and disposable CI runs only.
81: - The retired `MK_SKILL_ADVISOR_DB_DIR` name has no read site of its own.
82: - The retired name reaches this variable only in a process that runs the env alias bridge (`.skilled/hooks/shared/env-aliases.cjs`) before the read, and only while `SYSTEM_SKILL_ADVISOR_DB_DIR` is unset.
83: 
84: The override moves these advisor state files and the model server with the database, so a test or CI run keeps them out of the workspace and does not disturb the live advisor:
85: 
86: - **Generation file.** `skill-graph-generation.json` and its lock and temporary files live in the override directory instead of `.skilled/skills/.state/advisor/` (`runtime/lib/freshness/generation.ts`, `getSkillGraphGenerationPath`). Freshness pairs the counter with the database it describes, so a sandboxed daemon never marks the live advisor unavailable when it shuts down.
87: - **Quarantine store.** The watcher writes `skill-graph-quarantine.sqlite` in the override directory. The workspace default, the `.state/advisor` lease SQLite file, is unchanged, and an explicit store path still wins (`runtime/lib/daemon/watcher.ts`, `quarantineDbPath`).
88: - **Launcher state and bootstrap lock.** `.system-skill-advisor-launcher.json` and `.system-skill-advisor-launcher.lockdir` sit in the override directory instead of `runtime/database/` (`.skilled/bin/system-skill-advisor-launcher.cjs`, `refreshPaths()`).
89: - **Model server.** When no `HF_EMBED_SERVER_URL` is given, the launcher sets it to `hf-embed.sock` in the daemon's database-scoped IPC socket directory (`pinModelServerToAdvisorDatabase()`). A sandbox launcher never shares or signals the workspace model server. The pin is skipped when the IPC socket directory is a `tcp://` address.
90: - **Daemon child address.** With or without the override, when the parent sets no `HF_EMBED_SERVER_URL`, `createChildEnv()` gives the daemon child the socket the launcher's own model-server control arms. The child's embedding client reaches the server the launcher serves, even though the launcher sets the child's `SPECKIT_IPC_SOCKET_DIR` to the daemon's own socket directory.
91: 
92: Production and operator docs should treat the package-local path as the default. A runtime override must not be used to silently re-collocate the advisor DB with `system-spec-kit/runtime/database/`.
93: 
94: ### Child-process `MEMORY_DB_PATH` pointer
95: 
96: - `system-skill-advisor-launcher.cjs`'s `createChildEnv()` sets the advisor daemon child's `MEMORY_DB_PATH` (the env var `@spec-kit/shared/embeddings/factory.ts` reads to resolve which database's `active_embedder_*` pointer to use) explicitly to this policy's package-local `skill-graph.sqlite` path by default.
97: - A bare ambient `MEMORY_DB_PATH` in the parent process is never honored as an override, whoever set it, since that would silently re-collocate the advisor's embedder-pointer resolution with another package's database and defeat this policy's separation.
98: - To override for tests/CI only, set the dedicated `SYSTEM_SKILL_ADVISOR_MEMORY_DB_PATH` var instead.
99: 
100: ---
101: 
102: ## 5. MIGRATION NOTES
103: 
104: Current package state keeps the database under `runtime/database/` and serves it through the standalone daemon behind `node .skilled/bin/skill-advisor.cjs`.
105: 
106: The `skill_graph_*` handlers and the lower-level `lib/skill-graph/` database/query library are advisor-owned and package-local.

13: # Skill Graph Drift Reconciliation
14: 
15: When advisor status or validation points to stale graph state, this guide identifies the drift source and reconciliation path.
16: 
17: ---
18: 
19: ## 1. OVERVIEW
20: 
21: ### Purpose
22: 
23: Explains how to detect and reconcile drift between SQLite skill graph state and live `graph-metadata.json` source files.
24: 
25: ### When to Use
26: 
27: - `advisor_status`, `skill_graph_status` or `skill_graph_validate` reports stale or inconsistent graph state.
28: - A skill metadata edit is not reflected in query results.
29: - Operators need a rebuild sequence after source or database drift.
30: 
31: ### Core Principle
32: 
33: The SQLite graph is rebuildable runtime state; checked-in skill metadata remains the authored source of truth.
34: 
35: ### Key Sources
36: 
37: - [`freshness-contract.md`](../runtime/freshness-contract.md)
38: - [`daemon-lease-contract.md`](../runtime/daemon-lease-contract.md)
39: - [`skill-graph-query-cookbook.md`](./skill-graph-query-cookbook.md)
40: 
41: ---
42: 
43: ## 2. DRIFT SOURCES
44: 
45: The SQLite graph drifts from the source files when any of these happen:
46: 
47: 1. **Skill added**: a new `.skilled/skills/<name>/graph-metadata.json` appears on disk that the SQLite graph has not indexed yet.
48: 2. **Skill removed**: a skill directory is deleted but the SQLite graph still has rows for it.
49: 3. **Edge mutated**: an existing graph-metadata.json file changes its `edges.depends_on[]`, `edges.enhances[]` or `edges.conflicts[]` arrays but the SQLite graph holds stale edge rows.
50: 4. **Schema bump**: the JSON schema_version increments (1 → 2) but the SQLite graph still expects v1 fields.
51: 5. **Hash drift**: any file under `.skilled/skills/*/graph-metadata.json`, `.skilled/skills/*/SKILL.md` or `.skilled/skills/*/ROUTER.md` (where the skill carries one) changes, computed via SHA-256 hash. The daemon watches for hash changes per `freshness-contract.md` §5.
52: 
53: ---
54: 
55: ## 3. DETECTION
56: 
57: ### Via `skill_graph_status`
58: 
59: ```bash
60: node .skilled/bin/skill-advisor.cjs skill_graph_status --format json
61: ```
62: 
63: Inspect:
64: - `staleness.detectedAt` (ISO timestamp of last hash drift)
65: - `staleness.changedFiles[]` (array of source files that changed)
66: - `lastIndexedAt` (when SQLite was last rebuilt)
67: - `dbStatus` (`live`, `stale`, `absent`, `unavailable`)
68: 
69: If `dbStatus` is `stale` or `staleness.changedFiles[]` is non-empty, drift is present.
70: 
71: ### Via `skill_graph_validate`
72: 
73: ```bash
74: node .skilled/bin/skill-advisor.cjs skill_graph_validate --format json
75: ```
76: 
77: Returns structural integrity checks:
78: - `isValid` (boolean)
79: - `errors[]` (broken edges, schema violations, dependency cycles)
80: - `warnings[]` (missing reciprocals, asymmetric edges)
81: - `checkedNodes`, `checkedEdges` (counts)
82: 
83: A `false` for `isValid` plus broken-edge errors signal drift between SQLite graph plus source files.
84: 
85: ### Manual hash diff
86: 
87: ```bash
88: find .skilled/skills -name 'graph-metadata.json' -exec sha256sum {} + | sort
89: ```
90: 
91: Compare against the daemon's recorded signature stored alongside `runtime/database/.skill-graph.sig`. Mismatches indicate drift.
92: 
93: ---
94: 
95: ## 4. RECONCILIATION
96: 
97: Trust resolution fails closed. A call is untrusted unless `--trusted` or `SYSTEM_SKILL_ADVISOR_CLI_TRUSTED=1` is supplied. Mutation commands therefore require the maintainer path.
98: 
99: ### Standard reconciliation
100: 
101: ```bash
102: node .skilled/bin/skill-advisor.cjs advisor_rebuild --trusted --force true --format json
103: ```
104: 
105: Forces a full rebuild from source files. Generation counter bumps. Trust state transitions stale → live.
106: 
107: ### Index-only reconciliation
108: 
109: If you only want to re-index without bumping generation (advanced):
110: 
111: ```bash
112: node .skilled/bin/skill-advisor.cjs skill_graph_scan --trusted --json '{"skillsRoot":".skilled/skills"}' --format json
113: ```
114: 
115: Re-indexes the graph from source plus updates the hash signature.
116: 
117: ### Hard reset
118: 
119: If `advisor_rebuild` plus `skill_graph_scan` both fail:
120: 
121: ```bash
122: # Stop the advisor daemon first to release the lease
123: # Then:
124: rm -f .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/database/skill-graph.sqlite{,-wal,-shm}
125: rm -f .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/database/.skill-graph.sig
126: rm -f .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/database/.skill-graph.lease
127: # The next CLI call cold-starts the daemon, which recreates it from scratch.
128: ```
129: 
130: After hard reset, verify with `advisor_status` plus `skill_graph_validate` before trusting recommendations.
131: 
132: ---
133: 
134: ## 5. FAILURE MODES
135: 
136: | Failure | Symptom | Recovery |
137: |---|---|---|
138: | Rebuild succeeds but trustState stays stale | Generation counter not bumping | Inspect `advisor_status.generation`. If frozen, stop the daemon and let the next CLI call cold-start it. File a bug if reproducible |
139: | Source files unreadable (permission error) | `advisor_rebuild` errors with EACCES | Fix filesystem permissions on `.skilled/skills/*/graph-metadata.json`. The daemon needs read access |
140: | SQLite corruption mid-rebuild | `dbStatus` flips to `absent` after rebuild | Run hard reset procedure (§4) |
141: | Schema version mismatch (json v2, SQLite expects v1) | Validate reports schema-violation errors for new skills | Run `advisor_rebuild --force`. The rebuild applies any pending schema migrations |
142: | Hash signature corruption | Daemon refuses to detect drift (signature unreadable) | Delete `.skill-graph.sig`. Daemon regenerates on next scan |
143: | New skill added but never indexed | `skill_graph_query` returns empty for the new skill | Run `skill_graph_scan` manually. If still missing, verify the new graph-metadata.json passes JSON validation |
144: | Drift after `git pull` brings new graph-metadata.json files | Common after upstream sync | Run `advisor_rebuild --force` once after `git pull` to re-sync |
145: | Watcher fires repeatedly on the same file | Some editor saves trigger multiple change events | Daemon debounces (configurable). If debounce is too short, increase via `SYSTEM_SKILL_ADVISOR_WATCH_DEBOUNCE_MS` env var |
146: 
147: ---
148:

152: - [`daemon-lease-contract.md`](../runtime/daemon-lease-contract.md), lease must release cleanly for rebuild
153: - [`skill-graph-query-cookbook.md`](./skill-graph-query-cookbook.md), query the graph after reconciliation

13: # Skill Graph Propagate Enhances Tool
14: 
15: Open this reference when reviewing candidate `enhances` edges or deciding whether to apply them.
16: 
17: ---
18: 
19: ## 1. OVERVIEW
20: 
21: ### Purpose
22: 
23: Documents the internal `skill_graph_propagate_enhances` tool for detecting and optionally applying missing inbound `enhances` edges.
24: 
25: ### When to Use
26: 
27: - Auditing trusted-caller graph maintenance behavior.
28: - Reviewing candidate `enhances` edge propagation.
29: - Confirming why this tool is internal rather than a public hook path.
30: 
31: ### Core Principle
32: 
33: Enhance-edge propagation is a high-trust authoring helper: report first, write only with explicit trusted-caller intent.
34: 
35: ### Key Sources
36: 
37: - `runtime/handlers/skill-graph/propagate-enhances.ts`
38: - [`tool-ids-reference.md`](../runtime/tool-ids-reference.md)
39: - [Skill-root metadata contract](../../../sk-doc/sk-create-skill/references/shared/skill-root-metadata-contract.md)
40: 
41: ---
42: 
43: ## 2. DETECTION RULES
44: 
45: Three rules contribute to the composite confidence score with capped maximum contributions:
46: 
47: | Rule | Max Contribution | Condition |
48: |---|---|---|
49: | family-inference | 0.45 | Source skill already enhances many peers in target's family |
50: | asset-shape | 0.30 | Target has files or assets matching source's `enhance_when` rules |
51: | sibling-transitivity | 0.15 | Source enhances B and B has target as a sibling |
52: 
53: - **Family-inference** is the strongest signal and requires at least three existing `enhances` entries before it contributes.
54: - **Asset-shape** inspects the target skill's filesystem layout against the source's declared trigger shape.
55: - **Sibling-transitivity** walks one hop through known sibling links.
56: 
57: ---
58: 
59: ## 3. OPERATION MODES
60: 
61: Three modes control read-write behavior:
62: 
63: - `report` - Returns candidates without making any changes. This is the default.
64: - `propose` - Returns candidates without making any changes. Functionally an alias for `report`.
65: - `apply` - Writes selected candidates to source `graph-metadata.json` files.
66: 
67: - `apply` mode only writes candidates that are explicitly selected by ID or selected through `applyAllHighConfidence=true` for candidates above `minConfidence` (default 0.75).
68: - `dryRun` defaults to true so a fresh `apply` call without explicit `dryRun:false` still produces a no-write preview.
69: 
70: ---
71: 
72: ## 4. INVARIANTS
73: 
74: The tool enforces several invariants on every call:
75: 
76: - Trusted-caller authentication is required via `requireTrustedCaller`. Untrusted callers receive an authentication error before any detection runs.
77: - The workspace-escape guard resolves `skillsRoot` and verifies it stays under the current working directory. External absolute paths are rejected.
78: - The default mode is `report`. No writes occur unless `mode:'apply'` is set explicitly.
79: - The default `dryRun` is true. Writes only occur when `dryRun:false` is set explicitly.
80: - `apply` mode only writes candidates that match an explicit `applyCandidateIds[]` entry OR meet `minConfidence` when `applyAllHighConfidence=true`.
81: 
82: ---
83: 
84: ## 5. WHEN IT RUNS
85: 
86: The command is invoked manually through the CLI with a trusted caller context. It is not triggered automatically by other handlers or hooks.
87: 
88: Typical use cases:
89: 
90: - Maintenance sweeps that discover missing `enhances` relationships across a refactored skill set.
91: - Authoring assistance after adding a new skill that fits an existing family.
92: - Validation runs that report candidate edges without writing, so operators can review the proposal before applying.
93: 
94: The tool sits beside the eight other skill-graph tools as a low-frequency, high-trust authoring helper.

61: Three modes control read-write behavior:
62: 
63: - `report` - Returns candidates without making any changes. This is the default.
64: - `propose` - Returns candidates without making any changes. Functionally an alias for `report`.
65: - `apply` - Writes selected candidates to source `graph-metadata.json` files.
66: 
67: - `apply` mode only writes candidates that are explicitly selected by ID or selected through `applyAllHighConfidence=true` for candidates above `minConfidence` (default 0.75).
68: - `dryRun` defaults to true so a fresh `apply` call without explicit `dryRun:false` still produces a no-write preview.
69: 
70: ---
71: 
72: ## 4. INVARIANTS
73: 
74: The tool enforces several invariants on every call:
75: 
76: - Trusted-caller authentication is required via `requireTrustedCaller`. Untrusted callers receive an authentication error before any detection runs.
77: - The workspace-escape guard resolves `skillsRoot` and verifies it stays under the current working directory. External absolute paths are rejected.
78: - The default mode is `report`. No writes occur unless `mode:'apply'` is set explicitly.
79: - The default `dryRun` is true. Writes only occur when `dryRun:false` is set explicitly.
80: - `apply` mode only writes candidates that match an explicit `applyCandidateIds[]` entry OR meet `minConfidence` when `applyAllHighConfidence=true`.
81: 
82: ---
83: 
84: ## 5. WHEN IT RUNS
85: 
86: The command is invoked manually through the CLI with a trusted caller context. It is not triggered automatically by other handlers or hooks.
87: 
88: Typical use cases:
89: 
90: - Maintenance sweeps that discover missing `enhances` relationships across a refactored skill set.
91: - Authoring assistance after adding a new skill that fits an existing family.
92: - Validation runs that report candidate edges without writing, so operators can review the proposal before applying.
93: 
94: The tool sits beside the eight other skill-graph tools as a low-frequency, high-trust authoring helper.

12: 
13: # Skill Graph Query Cookbook
14: 
15: Use this cookbook while constructing or explaining a `skill_graph_query` call.
16: 
17: ---
18: 
19: ## 1. OVERVIEW
20: 
21: ### Purpose
22: 
23: Provides worked examples for every supported `skill_graph_query` query type.
24: 
25: ### When to Use
26: 
27: - Building or testing graph traversal calls.
28: - Explaining depends-on, enhances, conflict, hub, orphan or subgraph query output.
29: - Revalidating graph behavior after drift reconciliation.
30: 
31: ### Core Principle
32: 
33: Query examples should reflect live advisor semantics and remain tied to the package-local SQLite graph.
34: 
35: ### Key Sources
36: 
37: - [`tool-ids-reference.md`](../runtime/tool-ids-reference.md)
38: - [`db-path-policy.md`](../config/db-path-policy.md)
39: - [`skill-graph-drift.md`](./skill-graph-drift.md)
40: 
41: ---
42: 
43: ## 2. QUERY TYPE INDEX
44: 
45: | Query Type | Purpose | Worked Section |
46: |---|---|---|
47: | `depends_on` | Outbound dependencies of a skill | §3 |
48: | `dependents` | Inbound dependencies (reverse) | §4 |
49: | `enhances` | Skills this one enhances | §5 |
50: | `enhanced_by` | Skills that enhance this one | §6 |
51: | `family_members` | Sibling skills in the same family | §7 |
52: | `conflicts` | Skills marked as mutually exclusive | §8 |
53: | `transitive_path` | Path between two skills through edges | §9 |
54: | `hub_skills` | Skills with highest in or out degree | §10 |
55: | `orphans` | Skills with no edges in either direction | §11 |
56: | `subgraph` | Local neighborhood around a skill | §12 |
57: 
58: ---
59: 
60: ## 3. `depends_on`
61: 
62: **Purpose**: Returns the outbound `depends_on` edges declared in a skill graph-metadata.json `edges.depends_on[]` array.
63: 
64: **Input**:
65: 
66: ```json
67: { "queryType": "depends_on", "skillId": "system-skill-advisor" }
68: ```
69: 
70: **Output shape**:
71: 
72: ```json
73: {
74:   "queryType": "depends_on",
75:   "skillId": "system-skill-advisor",
76:   "relationships": []
77: }
78: ```
79: 
80: **Worked example**: `system-skill-advisor` currently has no hard dependencies. Query returns an empty edge list from the source graph-metadata.json.
81: 
82: **Gotcha**: An empty `relationships[]` does not mean the skill has no upstream needs. Many skills rely on `system-spec-kit` implicitly through the validate workflow without declaring it as a hard dependency. Cross-reference with the manual_testing_playbook for the runtime dependency story.
83: 
84: ---
85: 
86: ## 4. `dependents`
87: 
88: **Purpose**: Reverse query. Returns skills that declare `depends_on` pointing to the queried skill.
89: 
90: **Input**:
91: 
92: ```json
93: { "queryType": "dependents", "skillId": "system-spec-kit" }
94: ```
95: 
96: **Output shape**:
97: 
98: ```json
99: {
100:   "queryType": "dependents",
101:   "skillId": "system-spec-kit",
102:   "relationships": [
103:     { "source": "sk-code", "weight": 0.8, "context": "validation workflow" },
104:     { "source": "sk-doc", "weight": 0.6, "context": "template engine" }
105:   ]
106: }
107: ```
108: 
109: **Worked example**: `system-spec-kit` is the platform anchor. Most `sk-*` skills declare it as a dependency. Query returns the full inbound dependency list with each source skill's weight and context.
110: 
111: **Gotcha**: A high inbound count signals a hub. If you plan to change `system-spec-kit` public surface, run `dependents` first to size the blast radius before any commit.
112: 
113: ---
114: 
115: ## 5. `enhances`
116: 
117: **Purpose**: Returns outbound `enhances` edges from the queried skill's graph-metadata.json `edges.enhances[]` array.
118: 
119: **Input**:
120: 
121: ```json
122: { "queryType": "enhances", "skillId": "system-skill-advisor" }
123: ```
124: 
125: **Output shape**:
126: 
127: ```json
128: {
129:   "queryType": "enhances",
130:   "skillId": "system-skill-advisor",
131:   "relationships": [
132:     { "target": "cli-claude-code", "weight": 0.7, "context": "routes claude delegation requests" },
133:     { "target": "cli-opencode", "weight": 0.7, "context": "routes opencode delegation requests" }
134:   ]
135: }
136: ```
137: 
138: **Worked example**: The advisor enhances each CLI skill by routing prompts to the right one. Query returns the outbound enhancement edges, each carrying a context string explaining the relationship.
139: 
140: **Gotcha**: Asymmetric `enhances` declarations are common. A skill can declare it enhances another without that other declaring `enhanced_by`. The propagate-enhances internal tool (see [`propagate-enhances.md`](./propagate-enhances.md)) detects and proposes the missing reciprocals.
141: 
142: ---
143: 
144: ## 6. `enhanced_by`
145: 
146: **Purpose**: Inverse of `enhances`. Returns skills that declare they enhance the queried skill.
147: 
148: **Input**:
149: 
150: ```json
151: { "queryType": "enhanced_by", "skillId": "sk-code" }
152: ```
153: 
154: **Output shape**:
155: 
156: ```json
157: {
158:   "queryType": "enhanced_by",
159:   "skillId": "sk-code",
160:   "relationships": [
161:     { "source": "system-skill-advisor", "weight": 0.7, "context": "routes implementation requests" }
162:   ]
163: }
164: ```
165: 
166: **Worked example**: `sk-code` is enhanced by the advisor that routes implementation prompts to it. Query returns the inbound enhancement edges.
167: 
168: **Gotcha**: The result reflects only declared inbound edges. Run `skill_graph_propagate_enhances` in `report` mode to find skills that should be enhancing this one but have not declared the edge yet.
169: 
170: ---
171: 
172: ## 7. `family_members`
173: 
174: **Purpose**: Returns all skills sharing the same `family` field in graph-metadata.json.
175: 
176: **Input**:
177: 
178: ```json
179: { "queryType": "family_members", "family": "system" }
180: ```
181: 
182: **Output shape**:
183: 
184: ```json
185: {
186:   "queryType": "family_members",
187:   "family": "system",
188:   "members": [
189:     { "skillId": "system-spec-kit", "category": "system" },
190:     { "skillId": "system-skill-advisor", "category": "system" }
191:   ]
192: }
193: ```
194: 
195: **Worked example**: The `system` family contains the three first-party `system-*` skills. Query returns all members with their categories.
196: 
197: **Gotcha**: `family` is a soft grouping for navigation. It does not imply runtime dependencies. Use `depends_on` or `enhances` for the real causal edges.
198: 
199: ---
200: 
201: ## 8. `conflicts`
202: 
203: **Purpose**: Returns skills marked as mutually exclusive via `edges.conflicts[]` in graph-metadata.json.
204: 
205: **Input**:
206: 
207: ```json
208: { "queryType": "conflicts", "skillId": "cli-opencode" }
209: ```
210: 
211: **Output shape**:
212: 
213: ```json
214: {
215:   "queryType": "conflicts",
216:   "skillId": "cli-opencode",
217:   "relationships": []
218: }
219: ```
220: 
221: **Worked example**: Most cli-* skills do not declare conflicts. They route per dispatch and do not interfere. An empty result is the common case.
222: 
223: **Gotcha**: A non-empty `conflicts[]` signals a skill-level invariant. The advisor will refuse to surface both skills in the same recommendation set when conflicts are declared.
224: 
225: ---
226: 
227: ## 9. `transitive_path`
228: 
229: **Purpose**: Finds a path between two skills through any combination of edge types.
230: 
231: **Input**:
232: 
233: ```json
234: { "queryType": "transitive_path", "from": "system-skill-advisor", "to": "sk-code" }
235: ```
236: 
237: **Output shape**:
238: 
239: ```json
240: {
241:   "queryType": "transitive_path",
242:   "from": "system-skill-advisor",
243:   "to": "sk-code",
244:   "path": [
245:     { "skillId": "system-skill-advisor", "edge": "enhances", "weight": 0.7 },
246:     { "skillId": "sk-code", "edge": "(terminal)", "weight": null }
247:   ]
248: }
249: ```
250: 
251: **Worked example**: The advisor enhances sk-code directly. Path length is 1 hop. For deeper skills the path may include multiple edges of different types.
252: 
253: **Gotcha**: If no path exists the response returns `path: []`. BFS depth is capped at the runtime configured limit (typically 4 hops). Beyond that the query returns `path: []` even when a longer chain exists.
254: 
255: ---
256: 
257: ## 10. `hub_skills`
258: 
259: **Purpose**: Returns skills with the highest combined in plus out degree across all edge types.
260: 
261: **Input**:
262: 
263: ```json
264: { "queryType": "hub_skills", "topN": 5 }
265: ```
266: 
267: **Output shape**:
268: 
269: ```json
270: {
271:   "queryType": "hub_skills",
272:   "topN": 5,
273:   "skills": [
274:     { "skillId": "system-spec-kit", "inDegree": 18, "outDegree": 6, "total": 24 },
275:     { "skillId": "sk-doc", "inDegree": 12, "outDegree": 4, "total": 16 },
276:     { "skillId": "system-skill-advisor", "inDegree": 9, "outDegree": 7, "total": 16 }
277:   ]
278: }
279: ```
280: 
281: **Worked example**: `system-spec-kit` is the highest-degree hub because almost every other skill depends on its validation workflow. Use this query to identify high-blast-radius skills before refactors.
282: 
283: **Gotcha**: A high degree count does not mean a skill is high-quality. It just means many other skills point at it. Cross-reference with `advisor_validate` accuracy slices to see whether routing TO this skill is actually high-precision.
284: 
285: ---
286: 
287: ## 11. `orphans`
288: 
289: **Purpose**: Returns skills with zero edges in either direction.
290: 
291: **Input**:
292: 
293: ```json
294: { "queryType": "orphans" }
295: ```
296: 
297: **Output shape**:
298: 
299: ```json
300: {
301:   "queryType": "orphans",
302:   "skills": []
303: }
304: ```
305: 
306: **Worked example**: A healthy skill graph has zero orphans. Every skill should declare at least one outbound or inbound edge so the advisor can route to it via graph signals.
307: 
308: **Gotcha**: An orphan skill will still surface in `advisor_recommend` if its explicit_author or lexical lanes score high enough. But the graph_causal lane contribution will be zero. Orphans are a signal to add at least one edge in the skill graph-metadata.json.
309: 
310: ---
311: 
312: ## 12. `subgraph`
313: 
314: **Purpose**: Returns the local neighborhood around a skill (default radius 1, configurable).
315: 
316: **Input**:
317: 
318: ```json
319: { "queryType": "subgraph", "skillId": "system-skill-advisor", "radius": 2 }
320: ```
321: 
322: **Output shape**:
323: 
324: ```json
325: {
326:   "queryType": "subgraph",
327:   "skillId": "system-skill-advisor",
328:   "radius": 2,
329:   "graph": {
330:     "nodes": [
331:       { "skillId": "system-skill-advisor", "depth": 0 },
332:       { "skillId": "cli-claude-code", "depth": 1 }
333:     ],
334:     "edges": [
335:       { "source": "system-skill-advisor", "target": "cli-claude-code", "type": "enhances" }
336:     ]
337:   }
338: }
339: ```
340: 
341: **Worked example**: Use subgraph to build a visual neighborhood map around a skill before making changes. Radius 1 returns direct neighbors. Radius 2 includes neighbors of neighbors.
342: 
343: **Gotcha**: At radius 3 or higher the response can grow large for hub skills. The runtime caps the result at a configurable node count (default 100). Trim radius before requesting unless you need the full transitive closure.
344: 
345: ---
346: 
347: ## 13. RELATED
348: 
349: - [`tool-ids-reference.md`](../runtime/tool-ids-reference.md) §3, full `skill_graph_query` schema
350: - [`freshness-contract.md`](../runtime/freshness-contract.md), trust state must be `live` for reliable results
351: - [`propagate-enhances.md`](./propagate-enhances.md), internal tool that detects missing reciprocal enhances edges
352: - [`skill-graph-drift.md`](./skill-graph-drift.md), what to do when SQL graph diverges from graph-metadata.json source files
353: - `runtime/handlers/skill-graph/query.ts`, handler source

33: Query examples should reflect live advisor semantics and remain tied to the package-local SQLite graph.
34: 
35: ### Key Sources
36: 
37: - [`tool-ids-reference.md`](../runtime/tool-ids-reference.md)
38: - [`db-path-policy.md`](../config/db-path-policy.md)
39: - [`skill-graph-drift.md`](./skill-graph-drift.md)
40: 
41: ---
42: 
43: ## 2. QUERY TYPE INDEX
44: 
45: | Query Type | Purpose | Worked Section |
46: |---|---|---|
47: | `depends_on` | Outbound dependencies of a skill | §3 |
48: | `dependents` | Inbound dependencies (reverse) | §4 |
49: | `enhances` | Skills this one enhances | §5 |
50: | `enhanced_by` | Skills that enhance this one | §6 |
51: | `family_members` | Sibling skills in the same family | §7 |
52: | `conflicts` | Skills marked as mutually exclusive | §8 |
53: | `transitive_path` | Path between two skills through edges | §9 |
54: | `hub_skills` | Skills with highest in or out degree | §10 |
55: | `orphans` | Skills with no edges in either direction | §11 |
56: | `subgraph` | Local neighborhood around a skill | §12 |
57: 
58: ---
59: 
60: ## 3. `depends_on`
61: 
62: **Purpose**: Returns the outbound `depends_on` edges declared in a skill graph-metadata.json `edges.depends_on[]` array.
63: 
64: **Input**:
65: 
66: ```json
67: { "queryType": "depends_on", "skillId": "system-skill-advisor" }
68: ```
69: 
70: **Output shape**:
71: 
72: ```json
73: {
74:   "queryType": "depends_on",
75:   "skillId": "system-skill-advisor",
76:   "relationships": []
77: }
78: ```
79: 
80: **Worked example**: `system-skill-advisor` currently has no hard dependencies. Query returns an empty edge list from the source graph-metadata.json.
81: 
82: **Gotcha**: An empty `relationships[]` does not mean the skill has no upstream needs. Many skills rely on `system-spec-kit` implicitly through the validate workflow without declaring it as a hard dependency. Cross-reference with the manual_testing_playbook for the runtime dependency story.
83: 
84: ---
85: 
86: ## 4. `dependents`
87: 
88: **Purpose**: Reverse query. Returns skills that declare `depends_on` pointing to the queried skill.
89: 
90: **Input**:
91: 
92: ```json
93: { "queryType": "dependents", "skillId": "system-spec-kit" }
94: ```
95: 
96: **Output shape**:
97: 
98: ```json
99: {
100:   "queryType": "dependents",
101:   "skillId": "system-spec-kit",
102:   "relationships": [
103:     { "source": "sk-code", "weight": 0.8, "context": "validation workflow" },
104:     { "source": "sk-doc", "weight": 0.6, "context": "template engine" }
105:   ]
106: }
107: ```
108: 
109: **Worked example**: `system-spec-kit` is the platform anchor. Most `sk-*` skills declare it as a dependency. Query returns the full inbound dependency list with each source skill's weight and context.
110: 
111: **Gotcha**: A high inbound count signals a hub. If you plan to change `system-spec-kit` public surface, run `dependents` first to size the blast radius before any commit.
112: 
113: ---
114: 
115: ## 5. `enhances`
116: 
117: **Purpose**: Returns outbound `enhances` edges from the queried skill's graph-metadata.json `edges.enhances[]` array.
118: 
119: **Input**:
120: 
121: ```json
122: { "queryType": "enhances", "skillId": "system-skill-advisor" }
123: ```
124: 
125: **Output shape**:
126: 
127: ```json
128: {
129:   "queryType": "enhances",
130:   "skillId": "system-skill-advisor",
131:   "relationships": [
132:     { "target": "cli-claude-code", "weight": 0.7, "context": "routes claude delegation requests" },
133:     { "target": "cli-opencode", "weight": 0.7, "context": "routes opencode delegation requests" }
134:   ]
135: }
136: ```
137: 
138: **Worked example**: The advisor enhances each CLI skill by routing prompts to the right one. Query returns the outbound enhancement edges, each carrying a context string explaining the relationship.
139: 
140: **Gotcha**: Asymmetric `enhances` declarations are common. A skill can declare it enhances another without that other declaring `enhanced_by`. The propagate-enhances internal tool (see [`propagate-enhances.md`](./propagate-enhances.md)) detects and proposes the missing reciprocals.
141: 
142: ---
143: 
144: ## 6. `enhanced_by`
145: 
146: **Purpose**: Inverse of `enhances`. Returns skills that declare they enhance the queried skill.
147: 
148: **Input**:
149: 
150: ```json
151: { "queryType": "enhanced_by", "skillId": "sk-code" }
152: ```
153: 
154: **Output shape**:
155: 
156: ```json
157: {
158:   "queryType": "enhanced_by",
159:   "skillId": "sk-code",
160:   "relationships": [
161:     { "source": "system-skill-advisor", "weight": 0.7, "context": "routes implementation requests" }
162:   ]
163: }
164: ```
165: 
166: **Worked example**: `sk-code` is enhanced by the advisor that routes implementation prompts to it. Query returns the inbound enhancement edges.
167: 
168: **Gotcha**: The result reflects only declared inbound edges. Run `skill_graph_propagate_enhances` in `report` mode to find skills that should be enhancing this one but have not declared the edge yet.
169: 
170: ---
171: 
172: ## 7. `family_members`
173: 
174: **Purpose**: Returns all skills sharing the same `family` field in graph-metadata.json.
175: 
176: **Input**:
177: 
178: ```json
179: { "queryType": "family_members", "family": "system" }
180: ```
181: 
182: **Output shape**:
183: 
184: ```json
185: {
186:   "queryType": "family_members",
187:   "family": "system",
188:   "members": [
189:     { "skillId": "system-spec-kit", "category": "system" },
190:     { "skillId": "system-skill-advisor", "category": "system" }
191:   ]
192: }
193: ```
194: 
195: **Worked example**: The `system` family contains the three first-party `system-*` skills. Query returns all members with their categories.
196: 
197: **Gotcha**: `family` is a soft grouping for navigation. It does not imply runtime dependencies. Use `depends_on` or `enhances` for the real causal edges.
198: 
199: ---
200: 
201: ## 8. `conflicts`
202: 
203: **Purpose**: Returns skills marked as mutually exclusive via `edges.conflicts[]` in graph-metadata.json.
204: 
205: **Input**:
206: 
207: ```json
208: { "queryType": "conflicts", "skillId": "cli-opencode" }
209: ```
210: 
211: **Output shape**:
212: 
213: ```json
214: {
215:   "queryType": "conflicts",
216:   "skillId": "cli-opencode",
217:   "relationships": []
218: }
219: ```
220: 
221: **Worked example**: Most cli-* skills do not declare conflicts. They route per dispatch and do not interfere. An empty result is the common case.
222: 
223: **Gotcha**: A non-empty `conflicts[]` signals a skill-level invariant. The advisor will refuse to surface both skills in the same recommendation set when conflicts are declared.
224: 
225: ---
226: 
227: ## 9. `transitive_path`
228: 
229: **Purpose**: Finds a path between two skills through any combination of edge types.
230: 
231: **Input**:
232: 
233: ```json
234: { "queryType": "transitive_path", "from": "system-skill-advisor", "to": "sk-code" }
235: ```
236: 
237: **Output shape**:
238: 
239: ```json
240: {
241:   "queryType": "transitive_path",
242:   "from": "system-skill-advisor",
243:   "to": "sk-code",
244:   "path": [
245:     { "skillId": "system-skill-advisor", "edge": "enhances", "weight": 0.7 },
246:     { "skillId": "sk-code", "edge": "(terminal)", "weight": null }
247:   ]
248: }
249: ```
250: 
251: **Worked example**: The advisor enhances sk-code directly. Path length is 1 hop. For deeper skills the path may include multiple edges of different types.
252: 
253: **Gotcha**: If no path exists the response returns `path: []`. BFS depth is capped at the runtime configured limit (typically 4 hops). Beyond that the query returns `path: []` even when a longer chain exists.
254: 
255: ---
256: 
257: ## 10. `hub_skills`
258: 
259: **Purpose**: Returns skills with the highest combined in plus out degree across all edge types.
260: 
261: **Input**:
262: 
263: ```json
264: { "queryType": "hub_skills", "topN": 5 }
265: ```
266: 
267: **Output shape**:
268: 
269: ```json
270: {
271:   "queryType": "hub_skills",
272:   "topN": 5,
273:   "skills": [
274:     { "skillId": "system-spec-kit", "inDegree": 18, "outDegree": 6, "total": 24 },
275:     { "skillId": "sk-doc", "inDegree": 12, "outDegree": 4, "total": 16 },
276:     { "skillId": "system-skill-advisor", "inDegree": 9, "outDegree": 7, "total": 16 }
277:   ]
278: }
279: ```
280: 
281: **Worked example**: `system-spec-kit` is the highest-degree hub because almost every other skill depends on its validation workflow. Use this query to identify high-blast-radius skills before refactors.
282: 
283: **Gotcha**: A high degree count does not mean a skill is high-quality. It just means many other skills point at it. Cross-reference with `advisor_validate` accuracy slices to see whether routing TO this skill is actually high-precision.
284: 
285: ---
286: 
287: ## 11. `orphans`
288: 
289: **Purpose**: Returns skills with zero edges in either direction.
290: 
291: **Input**:
292: 
293: ```json
294: { "queryType": "orphans" }
295: ```
296: 
297: **Output shape**:
298: 
299: ```json
300: {
301:   "queryType": "orphans",
302:   "skills": []
303: }
304: ```
305: 
306: **Worked example**: A healthy skill graph has zero orphans. Every skill should declare at least one outbound or inbound edge so the advisor can route to it via graph signals.
307: 
308: **Gotcha**: An orphan skill will still surface in `advisor_recommend` if its explicit_author or lexical lanes score high enough. But the graph_causal lane contribution will be zero. Orphans are a signal to add at least one edge in the skill graph-metadata.json.
309: 
310: ---
311: 
312: ## 12. `subgraph`
313: 
314: **Purpose**: Returns the local neighborhood around a skill (default radius 1, configurable).
315: 
316: **Input**:
317: 
318: ```json
319: { "queryType": "subgraph", "skillId": "system-skill-advisor", "radius": 2 }
320: ```
321: 
322: **Output shape**:
323: 
324: ```json
325: {
326:   "queryType": "subgraph",
327:   "skillId": "system-skill-advisor",
328:   "radius": 2,
329:   "graph": {
330:     "nodes": [
331:       { "skillId": "system-skill-advisor", "depth": 0 },
332:       { "skillId": "cli-claude-code", "depth": 1 }
333:     ],
334:     "edges": [
335:       { "source": "system-skill-advisor", "target": "cli-claude-code", "type": "enhances" }
336:     ]
337:   }
338: }
339: ```
340: 
341: **Worked example**: Use subgraph to build a visual neighborhood map around a skill before making changes. Radius 1 returns direct neighbors. Radius 2 includes neighbors of neighbors.
342: 
343: **Gotcha**: At radius 3 or higher the response can grow large for hub skills. The runtime caps the result at a configurable node count (default 100). Trim radius before requesting unless you need the full transitive closure.
344: 
345: ---
346: 
347: ## 13. RELATED
348: 
349: - [`tool-ids-reference.md`](../runtime/tool-ids-reference.md) §3, full `skill_graph_query` schema

351: - [`propagate-enhances.md`](./propagate-enhances.md), internal tool that detects missing reciprocal enhances edges
352: - [`skill-graph-drift.md`](./skill-graph-drift.md), what to do when SQL graph diverges from graph-metadata.json source files
353: - `runtime/handlers/skill-graph/query.ts`, handler source

13: # Contract: the skill advisor CLI front door
14: 
15: Open this contract when wiring a caller to an advisor capability through the CLI.
16: 
17: ## 1. OVERVIEW
18: 
19: <!-- HVR_REFERENCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-with-human-voice/references/hvr-rules.md -->
20: 
21: ### Purpose
22: 
23: Defines the CLI command, argument, output and failure contract callers may rely on.
24: 
25: ### When to Use
26: 
27: - Before invoking an advisor capability through the CLI.
28: - When deciding how to handle its response or exit code.
29: 
30: > The single entry point for every advisor capability. Callers read this rather than the CLI
31: > source. Field names and exit codes here are frozen: a change to either is a breaking change.
32: 
33: ---
34: 
35: ## 2. INVOCATION
36: 
37: ```
38: node .skilled/bin/skill-advisor.cjs <command> [--arg value ...] --format json
39: ```
40: 
41: The shim resolves the built CLI, verifies the build is current, and reaches the daemon over a
42: unix socket. It starts the daemon when none is listening.
43: 
44: `--format` takes `json`, `jsonl` or `text`. Callers parse `json`.
45: 
46: `--warm-only` starts or attaches to the daemon and returns without running a command. Use it at
47: session start so the first real call does not pay daemon start.
48: 
49: ---
50: 
51: ## 3. COMMANDS
52: 
53: Nine, each accepting three spellings: snake case, kebab case and camel case.
54: 
55: The three mutating commands require caller trust; an untrusted caller is
56: refused before anything is written.
57: 
58: | Command | Mutates | Required arguments |
59: |---------|---------|--------------------|
60: | `advisor_recommend` | no | `prompt` |
61: | `advisor_status` | no | `workspaceRoot` |
62: | `advisor_validate` | no | `confirmHeavyRun` |
63: | `advisor_rebuild` | **yes** | none |
64: | `skill_graph_query` | no | `queryType` |
65: | `skill_graph_status` | no | none |
66: | `skill_graph_validate` | no | none |
67: | `skill_graph_scan` | **yes** | none |
68: | `skill_graph_propagate_enhances` | **yes** unless `dryRun` | none |
69: 
70: Optional arguments per command come from the tool manifest and are printed by
71: `<command> --help`.
72: 
73: ---
74: 
75: ## 4. OUTPUT ENVELOPE
76: 
77: Success goes to stdout:
78: 
79: ```json
80: { "status": "ok", "data": { ... } }
81: ```
82: 
83: Failure goes to **stderr**, not stdout:
84: 
85: ```json
86: { "status": "error", "error": "<message>", "exitCode": <int> }
87: ```
88: 
89: Callers that read only stdout see nothing on failure. Read stdout, then fall back to stderr.
90: 
91: `data` is the command's own payload. For `advisor_recommend` a caller may rely on
92: `recommendations[]` with `skillId`, `score`, `confidence` and `uncertainty`, plus
93: `effectiveThresholds`. Anything not named here may change.
94: 
95: **Fields that are not stable across calls** and must never be compared or cached:
96: `timestamp`, `generatedAt`, `durationMs`, `latencyMs`, `checkedAt`, `lastLiveAt`, `updatedAt`,
97: `generation`, `cache.hit`, and the measured latency values under a validate slice.
98: 
99: `cache.hit` deserves its own warning: two identical calls return `false` then `true`, because the
100: daemon caches by prompt. It describes the cache, never the recommendation.
101: 
102: ---
103: 
104: ## 5. EXIT TAXONOMY
105: 
106: Five codes. A caller decides what to do from the code, not by parsing the message.
107: 
108: | Code | Meaning | What a caller should do |
109: |------|---------|-------------------------|
110: | 0 | Success | Read `data` |
111: | 1 | The handler raised | Treat as a failed call; do not retry blindly |
112: | 64 | Usage: unknown command, missing or invalid argument | Fix the call; retrying is pointless |
113: | 69 | Protocol: the daemon speaks a version this CLI does not | Stop, and report both versions |
114: | 75 | Retryable: daemon not ready, at capacity, or shutting down | Retry, or proceed without a recommendation |
115: 
116: 75 is the one that matters for prompt-time callers. The advisor is an accelerator, so a caller
117: that gets 75 continues without a recommendation rather than blocking.
118: 
119: ---
120: 
121: ## 6. FAILURE POSTURE
122: 
123: The advisor never blocks the caller. Every integration treats an absent recommendation as normal:
124: the prompt still goes through, the command still runs, the session still starts. A caller that
125: waits on the advisor, or fails because the advisor failed, is wired wrong.
126: 
127: Set a timeout. The prompt-time integrations use a few seconds and fall through on expiry.
128: 
129: ---
130: 
131: ## 7. WHAT IS PROVEN ABOUT THIS SURFACE
132: 
133: A parity harness recorded 22 frozen cases across all nine commands against the CLI and against the
134: MCP surface while both shipped. Every success path returned identical payloads apart from
135: `cache.hit`, which differs only because whichever surface runs second hits the cache the first one
136: warmed; error envelopes differed by design, because an exit code is a thing only a process has.
